newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end at another SMI record.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end at another SMI record.

text.p: Swiss shares extended the week's gains and the SMI closed at another record high on Tuesday.
Dealers said technical factors, demand from foreign investors, a generally favourable interest rate environment and a weaker dollar helped boost sentiment during the session.
But uncertainties about the development of U.S interest rates could stop the upward trend, one dealer said.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) added 12.2 points or 0.26 percent to a record closing 4,752.3 points.
The broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) rose 16.13 points or 0.54 percent to 3,006.44 points.
ABB, whose first quarter net profit rose eight percent to $236 million, was a positive surprise, dealers said. ABB, ex-dividend of 38 francs, added seven francs to 1,755.
Cyclical stocks like Sulzer and Saurer were in demand. Sulzer, ex-dividend of twelve francs, rose five francs to 1,020.
Roche continued Monday's recovery, rising 160 francs to 12,060.
Novartis consolidated. falling nine francs to 1,876.
UBS, ex-dividend of 32 francs, fell 24 francs to 1,310.
Nokia Millefer rose 24 francs to 582. Turnover and orders intake for the first quarter were higher than expected, a spokesman of the group said.
SEZ fell after profit-taking 50 francs to 2,700. The group said it expected a substantial rise in sales in 1997.
